items.title: No local timing of the pathway
items.whyItMatters: The programme knows the end result (41 percent) but not where the days go; a value stream map needs timed steps.
items.opportunity: Time each step for a sample of children in four schools before any change.

items.title: Consent barriers by home language are unmeasured
items.whyItMatters: Families with limited majority-language proficiency return fewer forms (c5); an average improvement could hide them.
items.opportunity: Record home language and report the primary measure by it; include these families in conversations with interpreters.

items.title: Front-tooth staining may cause refusals the numbers misread
items.whyItMatters: Most parents find front-tooth staining unacceptable (c3); a fall in uptake could reflect informed refusal, not a failed pathway.
items.opportunity: Count informed refusals separately and explore them in conversations.

items.title: Numbers and views could be blended into one verdict
items.whyItMatters: Mixing strands invites claiming success from one while ignoring the other.
items.opportunity: Pre-specify one primary measure per strand and report them side by side before any integration.

items.title: Teachers and office staff are not part of the pathway design
items.whyItMatters: Changes to calls from class and form handling depend on them (retrieved teacher accounts).
items.opportunity: Include a teacher and an office staff member in the value stream mapping session.

errorsFound: The spring figure of 41 percent measures SDF at the next clinic visit, not within a fixed window; the new measure must state its window and denominator.
reevaluation: The gaps support a lean redesign with timed baseline mapping, a quantitative strand reported by home language, and a separate conversation strand.
summary: Five gaps; missing timings and unmeasured language barriers are high severity.
